lead.headline: 3 of 748 big credit unions lost 20%+ of net worth in a year: Civic, Greater Nevada, U.S. Eagle
lead.number: Net worth -39.5% (Civic FCU, $3.19B), -30.3% (Greater Nevada CU, ratio 3.33%), -20.6% (U.S. Eagle FCU); they rank #2, #4 and #1 of 758 on loans 60+ days late.
lead.watch_out: The late-loan rank isn't a second witness (same call report, same mechanism) and the ACCT_041B label is unconfirmed; Greater Nevada is profitable with low charge-offs yet lost $24.5M of net worth, unexplained.

sources.page_context: Civic Federal Credit Union loss widens, membership falls February 10, 2026 12:05 am The exchange for the debt economy Source: site The financial performance and membership of Civic Federal Credit Union veered in the wrong direction last year after it emerged as an independent financial institution. Raleigh-based Civic posted a net loss of $123.7 million in the 12 months ended Dec. 31, widening from a loss of $75 million in the first nine months of the year, according to recent federal regulatory filings. Its assets declined to $3.3 billion from $4 billion at the end of 2024 while membership sank 12.8%, or 52,345, to 355,581. The faltering results defied the expectations of Civic’s leadership as they prepared for the early June merger of the institution with Local Government Federal Credit Union, also based in Raleigh.
